archetype.name: Pocket Passer (rhythm distributor)
archetype.definition: A stationary, on-schedule thrower who wins by getting the ball out on time to a deep cast of targets from a well-run, under-center-friendly offense, with essentially nothing added as a runner.

report.headline: Top-six efficiency built partly on catch-up volume and an unsustainable intermediate spike
report.take:
Goff is the same quarterback he has been for most of his Detroit run: a timing passer who lives in structure, rarely runs (16 rushing yards on 10 carries), and turns a strong supporting cast into points. He sits sixth in EPA per dropback at 0.323, which tops even his 2024 peak of 0.293 and well clears last year's 0.157. He leads the position in avoided interceptions and fumbles lost, and his 12 touchdowns rank second. The tracking data shows a small shift in how he is getting there. His aggressiveness is at 19.4% tight-window throws, against a career band of roughly 11-13%. His intended air yards of 8.45 are also above the 6.8 aDOT of the last two seasons. He is pushing the ball more and getting paid for it.

The engine is the 10-19 yard window. On 47 throws there he is averaging 0.965 EPA, nearly a point per throw. Add 1.232 on 15 deep attempts, and Sam LaPorta (0.854 EPA per target) and Jameson Williams (0.705) have been the explosive outlets. Amon-Ra St. Brown has soaked up 57 targets at a modest 0.189. The short game is solid rather than spectacular at 0.153. The screen and behind-the-line game has been a drag, at negative EPA and a -16.1 CPOE.

Two things in the numbers flatter him. First, 64 of his 207 dropbacks came trailing by nine or more, where he has produced 0.418 EPA a play. In one-score states he is at 0.167: still good, but a top-12 quarterback rather than a top-6 one. That trailing volume comes from a defense ranked 31st in EPA. It is why all five Lions games went over, and why he threw 52 times for 412 yards in the Carolina loss. Second, the clean turnover sheet is partly luck. He has zero interceptions while throwing into tight windows at a career-high rate with an 11.5% bad-throw rate, and four turnover-worthy fumbles with none lost. He has thrown 8-16 picks every full season since 2018. Third down is also a genuine soft spot: -0.034 EPA, a -10.1 CPOE and a 36.7% conversion rate, with four of his 11 sacks.

Where it heads: the volume is real, because this defense will keep forcing him to throw. The efficiency should drift from elite toward very good as the intermediate EPA normalizes and a few interceptions arrive. Four of his five opponents rank 21st or worse on defense today. The one good one, the Jets at seventh, still got a 25-of-32, 12.1-EPA day. That is the best evidence the floor is high.

strengths.title: Intermediate and downfield hits
strengths.body: Throws of 10-19 air yards are producing nearly a point per attempt, and the deep shots are paying off too. LaPorta and Williams are winning in those zones. His rising aggressiveness and air yards say this is partly a deliberate shift, not just random catches. The direction is real, but a 0.965 EPA on 47 throws is far above anything sustainable and will come down.

strengths.title: Red-zone finishing
strengths.body: He has nine touchdowns on 40 red-zone attempts without a turnover. That is a big part of ranking second in passing touchdowns. Detroit's offense ranks third in EPA and fifth in success rate, so the red-zone trips should keep coming. The conversion rate may cool slightly.

strengths.title: Steady weekly floor
strengths.body: After a modest opener, every game has cleared 12 EPA passing. That includes the Jets, who rank seventh in defense. The career line backs it: he has been a top-16 EPA passer in four straight seasons. This is a well-established player in a stable situation, not a hot streak from a new role.

concerns.title: Turnover luck will not hold
concerns.body: Zero interceptions is the best mark in the league. It comes alongside a career-high tight-window rate, an 11.5% bad-throw rate ranked 17th, and four turnover-worthy fumbles that were all recovered. His history is 8-16 interceptions a season. Expect turnovers to show up, and the EPA with them.

concerns.title: Efficiency padded by catch-up states
concerns.body: Nearly a third of his dropbacks came down two scores, where he has averaged 0.418 EPA. In one-score games he is at 0.167. That is still good, but it is a different tier. His 31st-ranked defense keeps manufacturing those soft, high-volume situations. It helps his counting stats and inflates the efficiency picture.

concerns.title: Third down and a thin interior line
concerns.body: On third down he has been below average at -0.034 EPA, with a -10.1 CPOE and a 36.7% conversion rate. Part of that is long yardage, averaging 7.7 to go. Interior protection is also shaky. Guard Ben Bartch (93% of snaps) is out, and center Cade Mays is on IR, both with return dates that land on game day. His 23.5% pressure-to-sack rate matches his career, so when the line leaks, he goes down rather than escapes.

trend.note: After a 5.9-EPA opener, he has posted 18.6, 12.1, 12.3 and 16.4 passing EPA, with no interceptions in any game. Yardage has swung with game script, from 206 against New Orleans to 412 when chasing Carolina.

nextGame.headline: Rested Goff meets a defense that rarely allows big plays
nextGame.body:
Green Bay is the type of defense that stresses what has driven his season. It ranks second in explosive pass rate allowed and 10th in pass EPA. Quarterbacks have managed only 12.4 PPR points and 219.2 yards a game against it, both top-seven marks. His efficiency has leaned on chunk throws to LaPorta and Williams, and a defense that caps explosives forces him into the methodical, third-down-heavy game where he has been weakest. The opening is at WR1: the role has scored 4.8 points over its average against Green Bay, at 0.57 EPA per target, both bottom-six ranks. If St. Brown is the focal point, this is where his 57 targets finally produce. WR2 and tight end are tougher draws. It is a home dome divisional game, and he comes off 14 days of rest.

Availability cuts both ways. Green Bay's front is depleted: Javon Hargrave (46% of snaps) is out with a torn Achilles, linebacker Edgerrin Cooper (83%) is on IR, rotational DT Anthony Campbell is out, and Micah Parsons has not played this season. That should ease the pressure that his own line injuries invite. Even so, Green Bay still ranks ninth in sack rate. On Detroit's side, whether Bartch and Mays return on schedule decides how clean the interior pocket is. On offense, Green Bay ranks dead last in rushing EPA and is missing its starting center, so it may struggle to sustain drives. That could reduce the catch-up volume that has propped up Goff's totals.

keyMatchups.title: Chunk passing vs. explosive-stingy secondary
keyMatchups.body: His intermediate and deep throws produced most of his value. Green Bay allows explosive passes at the second-lowest rate in the league. Expect a lower yards-per-attempt game, with more weight on completion volume and red-zone execution.

keyMatchups.title: St. Brown against a leaky WR1 role
keyMatchups.body: St. Brown leads the team in targets but sits at just 0.189 EPA per target. Green Bay has been beaten by top receivers more than by anyone else. If Goff feeds his alpha early, this is the cleanest efficiency path on the field.

keyMatchups.title: Depleted GB front vs. patched interior
keyMatchups.body: Green Bay loses two regular defensive starters in Hargrave and Cooper. Detroit may be missing its starting guard and center. His pressure-to-sack rate sits mid-pack at 23.5%, so whichever interior holds up decides how many drives stall on third-and-long.

nextGame.watch: How often he hits the 10-19 yard window against a defense that rarely gives it up. If it is closed, his day becomes third-down conversions, his weakest area.

restOfSeason.body:
The volume is safe. Detroit runs the third-best offense, passes slightly more than expected, and the 31st-ranked defense will keep putting him in shootouts. A 4,500-plus yard, 30-plus touchdown pace fits what he has done in each of the last three years. What should regress is the efficiency. Near-point-per-throw intermediate results, zero interceptions and four unpunished fumbles are not repeatable. The schedule so far has also been soft, with four of five opponents ranked 21st or worse defensively.

Expect him to settle around 0.18-0.24 EPA per dropback, which is still top-10 quality. Touchdowns should run closer to two a game than 2.4, and interceptions should arrive at something like his career rate. The interior line's health and LaPorta and Williams staying productive are what keep the ceiling high.
swingFactors: Return of Bartch and Mays to the interior line
Whether Detroit's defense keeps forcing catch-up scripts
Interception regression on a higher tight-window rate

bets.reason: Green Bay allows 219.2 yards a game to quarterbacks (7th) and is second in explosive pass rate allowed, which cuts into the chunk plays behind his yardage. Green Bay's league-worst run offense may also limit the catch-up script that inflated his totals.

He is averaging 2.4 touchdowns a game on a 6.3% TD rate, but Green Bay allows only 1.2 passing TDs a game to quarterbacks (5th) and 12.4 PPR points (3rd). He has gone over 2.5 in only two of five games.

Zero interceptions on 191 attempts sits against a career-high 19.4% tight-window rate, an 11.5% bad-throw rate and a 8-16 pick history in every full season since 2018. Regression is due, though nothing in Green Bay's profile specifically forces it.

confidence.note: Five games against a mostly soft schedule, but a long, stable career baseline in the same offense.
